1.explanation:
• cli.md shows how the `--parser markdown` flag is invoked from the command line to reproduce the formatting issue.  
• api.md explains how the Prettier JavaScript API handles Markdown parsing and printing, which is where frontmatter trimming may occur.  
• configuration.md and options.md document any available user options (e.g. `--prose-wrap`, `--insert-pragma`) that could influence how frontmatter and blank lines are treated.  
• plugins.md describes the internal Markdown plugin integration (remark) where YAML frontmatter is parsed and printed, so it’s critical for debugging blank‐line handling.  
• technical-details.md outlines Prettier’s overall parsing/printing architecture and explains how whitespace and blank lines are managed across languages, including frontmatter blocks—a must-read for tracing where blank lines may be getting dropped.
1.bug_scenario: When formatting a Markdown file whose YAML frontmatter contains intentional blank lines between top-level keys and list entries, Prettier 3.3.0 is collapsing or removing those empty lines. In the playground example we see the input frontmatter separated by blank lines before “portfolios” and within the “blogs” array, but after formatting with `--parser markdown`, all of those blank lines are stripped out. The buggy scenario revolves around the YAML frontmatter block delimiters (---), the key/value lines, the array items (e.g. docs:, portfolios:, blogs:), and the intentional blank lines between them.
